answer.answer: Audit-ready checkpoint completed. The import remains a verified, lossless audit record; the archive’s `23761620` claim is corrected to a two-axis source/game-data boundary; duplicate structured data was not installed as another canonical snapshot; only distinct player context and explicitly provenance-labeled overrides were promoted; and the rejected Flowworks study remains superseded audit history.

claims.value: The completed import records `Star Rupture Game Analysis.zip` as 21,674,717 bytes with SHA-256 `1a1c1ef0ae00905ced37f1221ab22c4b9268f2ebe17b7516e6c9cac67d7f6fa3`. It contained 123 archive entries including directories and 115 manifested files plus `CHECKSUMS.sha256`; `unzip -t` and every packaged SHA-256 passed. The original ZIP and verified extracted tree are retained losslessly at the ignored local `imports/star-rupture-game-analysis__20260708T190137Z/raw` boundary, while `MANIFEST.csv` and `CHECKSUMS.sha256` remain tracked for audit. The retained legacy SQLite, snapshot JSON, and workbook hashes are respectively `d9ffbae20414d9e05a5dc02a664c904bc2bf0b8d74c8ae427ee9e8dccf6669fc`, `373e0f0dc556ce9cc03120321356bf7ce85fc012ffd7b49ce1aac3e89e6abf59`, and `2cb9f89360b9a721b2f41771ac77643a0438cb27e96b4f84a161ba93e7e04263`. The package is private because it includes personalized save state, screenshots, conversation-derived decisions, and duplicate third-party data.

The archive capture boundary is `2026-07-08T19:01:37Z`; its source-site version and reliable numeric-data build identity were not recorded. Its repeated association with Steam build `23761620` is therefore corrected: `ea_u1_0.2.8_build_23761620` was only the latest public executable observed, not proven provenance for every archived number. The canonical two-axis boundary is the single snapshot `ea-u1-gv35118973__srdb-2.3.4__20260711T050230Z`, captured at `2026-07-11T05:02:30.009644Z`: source/game-data claim Update 1, internal game version `35118973`, dated `2026-04-09`, contextually mapped with `date_and_update_label_match` confidence to `ea_u1_0.2.0_build_22674441`; source axis SRDB `2.3.4`; latest public build observed at capture `ea_u1_0.2.8_build_23761620`. Archive reports remain legacy July 8 calculations until actually ported and rerun against that canonical snapshot; they must not be relabeled with its ID.

No second canonical game-data snapshot was created. The archive’s 468 items, 191 public buildings, 234 recipe definitions, 6 corporations, 77 Corporation levels, 121 export offers, 15 development upgrades, 3,259 map markers, 3,094 loot rows, and official-news subset were treated as semantic duplicates of the richer canonical RuptureOps corpus. The item comparison had 468 overlaps, 467 substantive matches, and zero unique items; all listed structured categories had zero unique definitions or rows. Only distinct material was selectively promoted: player-save baseline `rourke-update1-save-baseline__20260711`; six medium-confidence impure/pure Calcium, Titanium, and Wolfram Ore Excavator v2 associations to `mechanical-drill-tier2`; 15 medium-confidence consumable-effect assumptions carrying an explicit warning that they require first-party or in-game verification; consolidated player planning notes; and nine site/geography assets (`faraday-works-map.png`, `flowworks-proposed-site.png`, `grand-basin-build-pad.png`, `grand-basin-region.png`, `landerworks-map.png`, `world-map-central-corridor.png`, `world-map-named-sites.png`, `world-map-named-sites.svg`, and `world-map-overview.png`). Reconciliation also corrected the `airlock` item/building collision and normalized Training Corporation’s literal `$undefined` sentinel to null. Legacy reports and models remain only in the verified raw import until recomputed.

The complete 18-file `Flowworks Campaign Sizing - Levels 8 to 15` family is retained only as `superseded_audit_only` history. Its buffer-minimization approach, excessive output storage, and later three-Stabilizer/two-slow-press design were explicitly rejected and must not become current guidance. The July 11 active authority is the staged Flowworks plan, itself still a proposal (`planned_not_installed`, with construction unconfirmed): the 10-machine starter is 1 Titanium Excavator, 1 Wolfram Excavator, 1 Titanium Smelter, 1 Wolfram Smelter, 1 Titanium Rod v2, 1 Wolfram Powder v2, 1 Wolfram Plate v2, 1 Stabilizer, 1 Impeller, and 1 Turbine. The valve expansion adds 1 Titanium Smelter, 1 Titanium Sheet v2, 1 Titanium Beam, 1 Titanium Housing, 1 Nozzle, and 2 Valves; Pressure Tank preparation adds 2 Pumps. The second Stabilizer is deferred until before Scanner/levels 11–12, and one HRS v2 is reserved as an evidence-triggered recovery option only if imported-HRS recovery fails in practice. After the second Stabilizer, planned imports are HRS 54/min, Helium-3 72/min, Sulphuric Acid 56/min, Rotor 60/min, and Stator 10/min, totaling 252/min on one 480/min Rail v3 trunk before buffer smoothing.

answer.answer: Landmark-grounded checkpoint completed from the frozen corpus. Grand Basin is corrected to the basin immediately east of Mythic Cry; relational pins and coordinate frames remain explicitly separated.

claims.value: Current canonical state supersedes the older provisional Red Lake/Redleaf match: Grand Basin Reserve is the broad basin north of the active production corridor and immediately east of GRO “Mythic Cry,” with Mythic Cry in the mountains immediately west. The reserve is selected but not confirmed built, and its marker denotes the basin area rather than a future Core. Its northern/northwestern pad is broad and relatively flat; the first active campus should remain east of the mountain/POI terrain boundary, preserve a POI/cliff combat exclusion strip, and leave the Geo Scanner near `3059,2618` outside the first district.
source_paths: corpus/Topics/StarRupture/Player save - sites and freight network.md

claims.value: Flowworks (`FLW`) is a selected, not-confirmed-built Titanium/Wolfram mechanical Works between active Landerworks and Faraday: east/northeast of Landerworks and west/northwest of Faraday. It is a proposed footprint, not a placed Core. The Landerworks–Flowworks–Faraday dashed axis records this active-corridor relationship only; it is not surveyed rail geometry. The adopted freight concept is a single storage-yard spur from the Landerworks–Faraday through trunk, with Flowworks machinery never used as a transit path.
source_paths: corpus/Topics/StarRupture/Player save - sites and freight network.md

claims.value: Keep screenshot registration and SRDB coordinates in separate frames unless a transform is verified. Planning-note coordinates identify SRDB markers, whereas overview site pins were visually terrain-registered from player screenshots. Within the screenshot registration, Landerworks has a directly visible base pin; Faraday is terrain-registered rather than directly labeled in its crop; Flowworks is only a proposed footprint; Grand Basin’s pin marks a reserve area, not a Core; and Sunstone Station and Brimstone Utility have verified parent relationships but no exact registered pins. The site axis is relational and must not be interpreted as surveyed track geometry.

These are adopted satellite plans, not confirmed construction. The preferred first permanent Goethite source is the safer northwestern triple at approximately `1393–1464,1838–1891`, northwest of Mythic Cry/Grand Basin: build all three Laser Drills, merge them into one Goethite-only Cargo Dispatcher, receive 45 raw Ore/min through one Receiver, and buffer it in one 1,600-unit Storage Depot v2 before exact-rate processing. This is preferred over the closer west field around `1252–1472,2950–3282`, which overlaps scanner/hostile envelopes; a geographically separate fourth drill is only an empty-buffer fallback and requires its own Dispatcher/Receiver pair. The preferred first Oil source is approximately `1234,3760`, west/southwest of Mythic Cry/Grand Basin: one Oil Extractor and one Crude-only Dispatcher/Receiver pair deliver 10 Crude/min into one V2 buffer feeding one GB-A Refinery. Reserve but do not initially build a second Oil pair or Refinery, because one Refinery consumes the full 10 Crude/min source plus large Titanium and Calcium feeds; the marker around `1351,4473` is a separate site, not a same-pad extension. Raw Goethite and Crude are moved because they are compact at extraction and expand heavily in processing; process them beside Grand Basin consumers rather than consuming world-trunk capacity with expanded intermediates. Goethite and Oil may share a receiver yard but never a Cargo link, rail lane, or storage unit.

answer.answer: The inherited archive-import request has already been reconciled once. Treat the forks as replay attempts, preserve the dirty `main` worktree and in-progress `ios/` work, and continue from the existing import ledger without another promotion.

claims.value: Duplicate topology: task `019f52a5-72aa-7c11-853c-5de258361b42` handled general import and reconciliation; `019f52fa-6195-7701-96a2-da6ec7ef7a08` continued live exploration; its sibling forks `019f52fa-6917-78a3-b1e5-7e631263b4a5` (logistics) and `019f52fa-7180-7552-a3b1-09be4c3ee493` (exploration) inherited the same `Star Rupture Game Analysis.zip` request. These tasks are neither independent imports nor independent corroboration.

Replay identity is the immutable tuple of source archive `Star Rupture Game Analysis.zip`, SHA-256 `1a1c1ef0ae00905ced37f1221ab22c4b9268f2ebe17b7516e6c9cac67d7f6fa3`, and import ID `star-rupture-game-analysis__20260708T190137Z`, backed by the verified immutable source copy and promotion receipts. The archive is 21674717 bytes, has 115 manifested files, and was imported at `2026-07-11T19:54:52Z`; a matching replay must reopen the successful reconciliation instead of creating another import or promoting overlapping facts again.

Canonical output is one reconciliation into snapshot `ea-u1-gv35118973__srdb-2.3.4__20260711T050230Z`, not installation of the archive as a competing snapshot. The duplicated item, building, recipe, progression, export, map, loot, and official-news material stays unpromoted; only the distinct save model, six Ore Excavator v2 associations, consumable assumptions, nine site/geography assets, and provenance-labeled vault notes were promoted. The legacy reports retain their July 8 boundary until actually ported and rerun. Dirty-tree safety is mandatory: the observed branch was `main`, it already contained unrelated data-pipeline, import, model, and curated-source changes, and the in-progress native work was isolated in untracked `ios/`; no pre-existing dirty file may be reverted or silently absorbed into an iOS commit.

Use exactly one continuation checkpoint: the archive reconciliation is verified and complete under `star-rupture-game-analysis__20260708T190137Z`; duplicate forks must converge on that ledger and must not emit additional promotions. Separately, the frozen `2026-07-11 23:14 UTC` repository observation records native implementation as incomplete: no `@main` entry, no SwiftUI Mission Timeline view, no recorded `xcodebuild` or test success, no simulator/visual/interaction verification, and no signing or phone-install handoff. A continuing agent must first inspect live repository truth, preserve unrelated dirty work, then finish the app/UI entry path, regenerate or refresh the project, build and test, and verify Mission Timeline in the simulator before claiming completion.
